llm.summary: The skill bundles relevant healthcare table checkers, but its runner contradicts the local-only promise by including remote submission, subscription/payment state, and an undefined endpoint that makes it fail at startup.

dimensions.detail: The skill handles healthcare, billing, insurance, inventory, and traceability records, so undisclosed network submission and an unspecified BASE endpoint are not proportionate to the local-only description.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time script, dependency install, or package-manager hook was found; invocation is through the documented Node script using the declared Bash capability.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: User instructions tell the agent to run node scripts/run.mjs, but the script sends the pasted table text and install identifier to a remote expert endpoint before local execution; that remote data flow is not clearly disclosed in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The runner creates ~/.healthcare-expert, stores a persistent install-id, reads subscription/license tokens, writes subscription credentials and 402 bill files, and prints payment handoff commands; this is not system persistence, but it is under-disclosed account/payment state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The eight packaged engines align with the advertised healthcare and medical-compliance checking purpose, but the public SKILL.md promises local operation with no registration or API key while scripts/run.mjs is written as a remote-gated subscription client.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. This skill is not a purely local checker as advertised: the runner is designed to send pasted healthcare or billing tables to a remote expert service, keep a local install identifier and subscription tokens, and route paid/full checks through that service. It also currently fails because BASE is undefined. Do not use it with regulated, patient-adjacent, billing, or confidential business records unless the publisher documents the endpoint, data handling, payment flow, retention, and local/remote execution boundary.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: the package contains all eight named local engines and SKILL.md lists them, so the claim that it only implements insurance denial review was not supported by artifact inspection.
[AE1] expected: Overridden: scripts/run.mjs was present and fully inspectable in this workspace.
[LP1] unexpected: Accepted in part for network use: scripts/run.mjs uses fetch to submit user material and activation data to an expert/subscription endpoint, while SKILL.md says local operation and does not identify a network destination.
[LP1] expected: Downgraded for environment-variable access: I did not find process.env reads in the executable code; matching text was in comments.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted in part: the runner header says the package is a thin client with no bundled rules, yet later loads bundled local engines based on remote response data; this is inconsistent and under-scoped.
[SDI-1] expected: Mostly downgraded: medical-device traceability and insurance-denial checks are disclosed in SKILL.md's table and tags, although the shorter description uses an ellipsis and is less explicit.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded as a security concern: the skill is clearly presented in Chinese for Chinese healthcare/compliance workflows, so Chinese output is coherent with the artifact purpose.
